title: And Mastiansky with the old cither.
html_source: Bloom lists Julius Mastiansky as a suspected Molly suitor. So, Bloom thinks that he was interested in her and that is probably true. Matiansky’s wife also seemed wary of the younger Molly. However, it is clear from Molly’s monologue in the last chapter that she never had sex with him because all she knows about his sexual preferences (he prefers doggie-style and it does not appear that she has ever tried that position) she learns from conversations with his wife.
